issues.legal_issue: A gift of property by a husband to his minor wife may be completed through acceptance by her mother when no property guardian is available, provided the donor clearly intends to transfer the property and divests himself of ownership and possession.
material_facts: The husband executed a registered deed gifting property, including immovable property, to his wife, who was a minor at the time.
The wife’s father, grandfather, and the relevant executors who could act as guardians of her property were not available.
The wife was in her mother’s care, and the husband was residing in the mother’s home during his illness.
The mother accepted the gift and took possession on the minor wife’s behalf; the husband handed the deed to her.
The Court found that the deed and its delivery manifested a clear intention to transfer ownership and that the husband divested himself of ownership and possession.
The lower courts had held the gift invalid because the mother was not a legal guardian of the minor’s property.
issues.conclusion: The gift was valid and complete, and the appeal was allowed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Hanafi Muhammadan law, a hiba ordinarily requires a declaration, acceptance, and delivery of possession; registration alone does not cure the absence of possession. But where no legal guardian of a minor’s property is available, possession may be taken on the minor’s behalf by the mother or another person caring for the minor, provided the donor clearly intends an immediate transfer and divests himself of ownership and possession. The Court relied on the principles discussed in the Hedaya, Durrul-Mukhtar, Radd-ul-Mukhtar, Bahr-al-Raiq and Fatawa-i-Alamgiri, and on Mohammad Sadiq Ali Khan v. Fakhr Jahan, Md. Abdul Ghani v. Mt. Fakhr Jahan, Nabi Sab v. Papiah, Nawab Ian v. Safiur Rahman, Munni Bai v. Abdul Gani, Mt. Fatma v. Mt. Autun, Mst. Azizi v. Sona Mir, and Mareroad v. Kunhali. Suna Mia v. S.A.S. Pillai and Musa Miya v. Kadar Bux were distinguished because they concerned minors whose fathers were alive and competent.

rule.if: gift_validity_challenged_in_partition_proceeding and gift_is_from_husband_to_minor_wife and property_guardians_unavailable and mother_accepts_and_takes_possession_for_minor and clear_and_manifest_transfer_intent and donor_divests_ownership_and_possession

predicates.gift_validity_challenged_in_partition_pr: An heir challenged a gift as invalid in a proceeding seeking partition of the property.
predicates.gift_is_from_husband_to_minor_wife: A husband made a gift of property to his wife while she was a minor.
predicates.property_guardians_unavailable: The persons who could legally act as guardians of the minor’s property were unavailable.
predicates.mother_accepts_and_takes_possession_for_: The minor’s mother, who had the minor in her care, accepted the gift and took possession on the minor’s behalf.
predicates.clear_and_manifest_transfer_intent: The donor’s declaration and conduct clearly showed an intention to transfer the property immediately to the minor.
predicates.donor_divests_ownership_and_possession: The donor handed over the deed and relinquished ownership and possession of the gifted property.

issues.definition: In a partition proceeding challenging a husband’s gift to his minor wife, the gift is valid when no property guardian is available, her mother accepts and takes possession for her, the transfer intention is clear, and the husband gives up ownership and possession.
